questions.prompt: Which device can function as both input and output?
Which storage technology uses magnetised spinning platters?
Name the temporary storage area used when devices operate at different speeds.
Which statement about RAM is accurate?
questions.option_a: RAM retains all data with no power
questions.option_d: RAM stores data only on optical discs

questions.prompt: Explain why a printer may need a buffer when receiving a large document.
questions.model_answer: The computer can transmit data faster than the printer can output pages. A buffer temporarily stores the incoming data so the printer can retrieve it at its own rate.
questions.grading_criterion:
1: Identify a difference in data rates between sender and printer.
1: Explain that the buffer temporarily holds incoming data.
1: Explain how the printer uses buffered data as it becomes ready.
questions.student_guidance:
Compare the speeds of the two devices.
Describe where incoming information waits.
Describe how printing proceeds.

questions.prompt: Describe how a touchscreen ticket machine uses input, processing and output.
questions.model_answer: The touchscreen detects the passenger selection as input. The processor determines the fare or available route. The screen shows the result or a printer produces a ticket as output.
questions.grading_criterion:
1: Identify a suitable touchscreen input.
1: Describe a relevant processing action.
1: Identify a suitable output.
questions.student_guidance:
Think of the passenger’s action.
Think of the calculation or decision.
Think of what the passenger receives.
